def: The position of a byte in the program's addressable storage.
The number of bytes occupied by one stored element.
A distance in bytes from a stated starting point.
A typed value that can refer to an object, a function or just past an array, or be null.
A region of storage that an array interpretation reads and writes.
One independently indexed direction of an array.
The ordered list of element counts along the axes of an array.
The number of axes an array has.
The signed change in byte offset caused by increasing one axis index by one.
The byte offset reached when every index is zero.
Descriptions of how to interpret stored bytes, as opposed to the values themselves.
The type and size of each stored element, such as a four-byte signed integer.
An array with an ordered set of axes whose coordinates select stored elements.
A traversal in which the last axis index changes fastest and earlier axes change more slowly.
Laying out an array's logical elements in consecutive element-sized positions, with no gaps, in a stated traversal order.
An array interpretation that shares another object's storage instead of owning a copy.
Two or more descriptions that reach the same stored bytes, so a write through one is visible through the other.
A selection of positions along an axis using a starting index, a stopping point and a step.
A change of shape that preserves the element sequence in a stated traversal order.
Creating independently stored elements by reading a view in a stated traversal order.
Matching array shapes for an elementwise operation by reusing input elements instead of copying them.
A summary computed from visited values, used to check that a traversal read the expected data.
An access pattern in which nearby storage positions tend to be used close together in time.
The median of the absolute distances between individual samples and their median.
